info.title: assembly-differ: a dotnet tool to diff assemblies

commands.name: api
commands.description:
Writes the public API of a build as .api files, or checks
committed ones against it.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --output
options.description: Write the files to this directory, and remove the .api files there the API no longer has. [default: null]

options.name: --verify
options.description: Check that the .api files in this directory match the build, and exit with 5 when they do not. [default: null]

options.name: --split
options.description: Split each API into a file per namespace, or per namespace's first two parts, such as System.Collections, for large assemblies. [default: none] [allowed: none|namespace|top-level-namespace]

options.name: --format
options.description: text writes .api files; json prints the API with every part of each declaration as a field. [default: text] [allowed: text|json]

options.name: --target
options.description: [repeatable] Only these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one. [default: null]

options.name: --framework
options.description: Only this target framework, such as net8.0. [default: null]

options.name: --project
options.description: [repeatable] Read this project file, whatever kind it is. Repeat it for more than one. [default: null]

options.name: --include-tests
options.description: Read test projects too.

options.name: --include-unpackable
options.description: Read projects with IsPackable set to false too.

options.name: --reference
options.description:
[repeatable] Look in this directory for the assemblies an API refers to, such as a package's dependencies, so an enum default is written by name. Repeat it for more than one. Projects, and packages already in the packages folder, are found without it. [default: null]
Notes:
A .api file is the API as C#: an indented tree of namespaces, types and members, one declaration per line, with a
header that names the types from other assemblies. Commit them next to the code and a change to the API shows in
the pull request as a change to the file; --verify fails the build when they are out of date. Without a path it
reads the solution or projects in the current directory, as the projects command does, and takes each library's
Release build for every framework it targets; it does not build, so run dotnet build -c Release first. An assembly
whose frameworks have the same API gets one file; otherwise one per framework, such as MyLib.net8.0.api.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: A .dll, a directory of them, or a .nupkg. Defaults to the libraries in the current directory. [default: null]

commands.name: api-diff
commands.description:
Compares the .api files in two directories: what changed from
the old ones to the new ones, by path.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --format
options.description: text prints each change; json writes api-changes.json, with the APIs without changes too. [default: text] [allowed: text|json]

options.name: --output
options.description:
A file to write the json report to, besides the summary on the console. [default: null]
Notes:
Each API is compared with the one of the same name, so the files of one target framework are compared with the files
of the same framework. An API only the new directory has is added, a minor change, and one only the old directory
has is removed, a major one. Nothing is built, so it compares what two commits committed, such as the base of a
pull request and its head, and says what the pull request itself changes however much main has changed since the
last release. Always exits with 0 when it could compare; read the suggested version change from the report.

arguments.name: OLD_DIRECTORY
arguments.description: The directory of the earlier .api files, such as the base branch's api/.

arguments.name: NEW_DIRECTORY
arguments.description: The directory of the later .api files.

commands.name: files
commands.description:
Compares two local builds: dlls, directories of dlls, or .nupkg
files.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --framework
options.description: The target framework to take from a .nupkg, such as net8.0. Defaults to the newest both packages ship. [default: null]

options.name: --target
options.description: [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.

options.name: --format
options.description: The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]

options.name: --output
options.description: A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

arguments.name: OLD
arguments.description: The old build: a .dll, a directory or a .nupkg.

arguments.name: NEW
arguments.description: The new build: a .dll, a directory or a .nupkg.

commands.name: nuget
commands.description:
Compares two versions of a package; in a solution, the version
your projects use with another.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --framework
options.description: The target framework to compare, such as net8.0. In a solution, defaults to the one each project compiles against. [default: null]

options.name: --all
options.description: In a solution, show every change, not only the ones to API your built projects use.

options.name: --target
options.description: [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.

options.name: --format
options.description: The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]

options.name: --output
options.description: A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>
Notes:
In a directory with a solution or project files, nuget X compares the version of X your projects resolve with
its latest stable release, and nuget X 2.0.0 with 2.0.0: what updating would change. It reads the resolved version,
and the target framework each project compiles X for, from obj/project.assets.json, so restore first. When projects
resolve different versions, each is compared. In a solution it shows only the changes to the types and members your
built projects reference, the ones that affect you, unless --all is set; build first. Members match by name, and a
constant you use does not show, because the compiler copies its value into your code. Give two versions to compare
them anywhere.

arguments.name: VERSION
arguments.description: With one version, the version to update to; with two, the old one. [default: null]

arguments.name: NEW_VERSION
arguments.description: The new version, when the old one is given too. [default: null]

commands.name: projects
commands.description:
Compares every library project in the current directory with the
latest release of its package. Runs when no command is given.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --project
options.description: [repeatable] Compare this project file, whatever kind it is. Repeat it for more than one. [default: null]

options.name: --include-tests
options.description: Compare test projects too.

options.name: --include-unpackable
options.description: Compare projects with IsPackable set to false too.

options.name: --target
options.description: [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.

options.name: --format
options.description: The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]

options.name: --output
options.description: A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>
Notes:
It reads the one solution in the directory, or else the project files in it, and skips test projects and projects
with IsPackable set to false. It compares each project's Release build, for its newest target framework, with the
latest stable release of its package on the feeds your NuGet.config lists. It does not build: run
dotnet build -c Release first, and a project without build output is skipped with a warning. A project whose
package has no release yet is reported and skipped. It needs the .NET SDK, to read the projects.

commands.name: pull-request
commands.description:
Puts a report on the pull request a GitHub Actions run is for:
the job summary, one comment kept up to date, and the release
label for the suggested version change.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --repository
options.description: The repository as owner/name; defaults to GITHUB_REPOSITORY. [default: null]

options.name: --pull-request
options.description: The pull request number; defaults to the one in GITHUB_EVENT_PATH. [default: default]

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this, unless the pull request has the allow label; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

options.name: --allow-label
options.description: The label that allows a change at --fail-on, so the check passes; empty allows none. [default: breaking-allowed]

options.name: --major-label
options.description: The label for a Major change, matching release-drafter's; empty sets none. [default: breaking]

options.name: --minor-label
options.description: The label for a Minor change; empty sets none. [default: feature]

options.name: --patch-label
options.description: The label for a Patch change; empty sets none. [default: ]

options.name: --base-report
options.description: The api-changes.json of api-diff for this pull request against its base branch. When given, the labels and --fail-on follow this change, the pull request's own, and the report above is shown as the change since the last release, for information. [default: null]

options.name: --base-name
options.description: What the base is called in the comment, such as the branch and its pull request; used with --base-report. [default: null]

options.name: --stack
options.description: A json array of the pull requests below this one in a stack, each with number, title, url, suggestedVersionChange and breakingChanges, to say which introduced the changes since the last release; used with --base-report. [default: null]

options.name: --api-code
options.description: The exit code of api --verify, to put the check of the committed .api files in the same comment: 0 when they match the build, 5 when they do not. The check fails on anything else. [default: default]

options.name: --api-report
options.description: What api --verify printed, for the comment; used with --api-code. [default: null]

options.name: --no-comment
options.description: Leave the comment alone.

options.name: --no-labels
options.description:
Leave the labels alone.
Notes:
Run a command with --format json first; this reads the api-changes.json it writes. The comment is found again by a
hidden marker and updated, and the labels this tool set are recorded in it: a later run swaps only those, never a
label a person added. It needs GITHUB_TOKEN with pull-requests: write. Without write access, as on a pull request
from a fork, it writes the job summary, warns and succeeds; outside a pull request it writes the job summary only.
With --fail-on, a change at that level fails the check until someone adds the allow label, breaking-allowed by
default; the workflow has to run on the labeled and unlabeled events too, so adding the label runs it again.

arguments.name: REPORT
arguments.description: The api-changes.json a command wrote with --format json.

commands.name: release
commands.description: Compares a new build with the release before it.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --package
options.description: The package id; read from a .nupkg when not given. [default: null]

options.name: --version
options.description: The version being released; read from a .nupkg when not given. [default: null]

options.name: --framework
options.description: The target framework to compare, such as net8.0. Defaults to the newest the .nupkg ships. [default: null]

options.name: --require-baseline
options.description: Fail when there is no earlier release to compare with.

options.name: --all-assemblies
options.description: Compare every assembly the build ships, not only the ones the solution or projects in this directory build; -t overrides both.

options.name: --target
options.description: [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.

options.name: --format
options.description: The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]

options.name: --output
options.description: A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>
Notes:
Give a .nupkg and the package id and version come from it; for a .dll or a directory, pass --package and --version.
The release compared with is the newest stable one before that version, on the feeds your NuGet.config lists.
Without one, this is a first release: there is nothing to compare, and the command succeeds unless
--require-baseline is set.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: The new build: a .nupkg, a .dll or a directory.

commands.name: upgrades
commands.description:
Lists the packages a solution references that have a newer
release, and what updating each would break.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --all
options.description: Count every change, not only the ones to API your built projects use.

options.name: --format
options.description: markdown, a table, or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|json]

options.name: --output
options.description: A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console. [default: null]

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
Exit with code 4 when an update's change to the API your code uses is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
One of: <none|patch|minor|major>
Notes:
It reads the packages every project in the directory references directly, as obj/project.assets.json resolves them,
so restore first. Each one with a newer stable release on your NuGet.config feeds is compared with it, the way
nuget X is: only the changes to API your built projects use count, unless --all is set, so build first. Use
assembly-differ nuget X to see one package's changes in full.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version.
